name: Greens Bush Walk
address: Greens Bush, Mornington Peninsula National Park, VIC 3939
signature: The Peninsula's largest remnant bushland — ancient coastal scrub, significant birdlife, and genuine quiet in the middle of one of Victoria's most visited regions
editorNote:
Greens Bush is the most significant bushland remnant on the Mornington Peninsula — 1,100 hectares of ancient coastal scrub and heathland in the middle of Mornington Peninsula National Park. The walk network here is genuinely remote-feeling despite being minutes from Cape Schanck and Rosebud.

The main loop through the heath and scrub takes about 2.5 hours and is best in spring when the wildflowers are at their peak — banksias, wattles, and heaths in a succession that runs from August through November. The birdlife is exceptional year-round: honeyeaters, robins, and the occasional powerful owl at dusk.

This is the section of the Two Bays Walking Track between Arthurs Seat and Bushrangers Bay. Walking it as a standalone day section (park at the Boneo Rd entrance, walk in and back) is the most practical approach. No facilities, limited signage — download the Parks Victoria trail map before you go.
whyWeGo: The Peninsula at its most primeval — 1,100 hectares of ancient coastal scrub that most visitors never find.
ifOnlyOneThing: Go in September or October when the heath is flowering. Bring binoculars.
